Rashi on Pesachim 71a:10:1.english: To include the night of the last Festival day in rejoicing - Like the other nights of the Festival.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:10:2.english: Or is it only, etc. - As I explained.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:12:1.hebrew: לאימורי חגיגת ט"ו שנפסלין בלינה - ואע"פ שזמן אכילת בשרה כל יום המחרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:12:1.english: Regarding the sacrificial parts of the Festival offering of the fifteenth [of Nisan] that are disqualified [when left] overnight - Even though the time for eating its meat is all of the following day.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:12:2.english: And juxtaposed with it is "the first of the first fruits, etc." - And expound from it: [the] first morning.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:13:1.hebrew: דבשר איפסיל ליה מאורתא - משחשכה ועבר יום ששה עשר, ואימורין יכשרו עד בקר שבעה עשר. דאי בקר בקר שני — בקר של שבעה עשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:13:1.english: Where the meat is disqualified from the evening - Once it grows dark and the sixteenth day has passed, yet the sacrificial parts would be valid until the morning of the seventeenth. For if "morning" [meant] the second morning — [that would be] the morning of the seventeenth.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:14:1.hebrew: ר' אליעזר בן עזריה - בפרק בתרא (דף קכ:), דאמר מדאורייתא אכילת פסח עד חצות ותו לא:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:14:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Azaryah - In the last chapter (120b), where he says [that] by Torah law the eating of the Paschal offering is until midnight, and no longer.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:15:1.hebrew: הכי קשיא ליה - אע"ג דאותיב מלתא אחריתי:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:15:1.english: This is what was difficult to him - Even though he raised an objection [with] another matter.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:15:2.hebrew: ומי איכא מידי - כלומר, אפשר להיות משמעות המקרא בקר שני? אנן חזינן תנא דמתנית' דלקמן, דאפי' לבשר שהוא קל מאימורין, לא בעי "ראשית", ו"בקר" דכתיב ביה משמע ליה לתנא בקר ראשון; ורב כהנא באימורין, דחמירא קדושתיהו, לא משמע ליה "בקר" דכתיב גבייהו בקר ראשון בלא "ראשית":
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:15:2.english: And is there anything - That is to say, could the meaning of the verse be the second morning? We see [the] tanna of the baraita below, that even for meat, which is more lenient than sacrificial portions, he does not require [the word] "first," and [the word] "morning" that is written regarding it means to the tanna the first morning; whereas [for] Rav Kahana, regarding sacrificial portions, whose sanctity is more stringent, [the word] "morning" that is written regarding them does not mean to him the first morning without [the word] "first."

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:16:1.hebrew: אשר תזבח בערב - בחגיגת ארבעה עשר מיירי, דנשחטת עם הפסח בערב, דהא ליכא למימר בערב של יום טוב הראשון עצמו קאמר קרא; דאם כן, מאי "בערב"? הלא שחיטתן ביום כולו:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:16:1.english: That you sacrifice at evening - [The verse] is speaking of the festival offering of the fourteenth [of Nisan], which is slaughtered with the Paschal offering in the evening. For you cannot say [that] the verse is speaking of the evening of the first day of the festival itself, for if so, what is [meant by] "at evening"? Is their slaughtering not throughout the entire day?

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:1:1.english: At the time of rejoicing - on the Festival, which is a time of rejoicing.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:2:1.hebrew: והיית אך שמח - קרא יתירא הוא, דכתיב לעיל מיניה: "חג הסוכות תעשה לך שבעת ימים", וסמיך ליה: "ושמחת בחגך", והדר כתיב: "שבעת ימים תחוג וגו' והיית אך שמח":
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:2:1.english: And you shall be but joyous - [This] is a superfluous verse, for it is written above it: "You shall make for yourself the Festival of Sukkot for seven days," and juxtaposed to it: "And you shall rejoice in your Festival," and then it is written: "Seven days shall you celebrate, etc., and you shall be but joyous."

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:2:2.hebrew: לרבות לילי יום טוב האחרון - ואין שמחה אלא באכילת שלמים. ויום טוב האחרון גופיה לא, דהא תרי זימני שבעת ימים כתיב גבי שמחה כדפרישי', וממילא אימעיט שמיני:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:2:2.english: To include the night of the last Festival day - And rejoicing is only through eating peace-offerings. But the last Festival day itself is not [included], for "seven days" is written twice regarding rejoicing, as I explained, and consequently the eighth [day] is excluded.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:2:3.hebrew: או אינו אלא לרבות לילי יום טוב הראשון - ואף על פי שאין קרבן בלילה, נלמד שהטעינו הכתוב לשחוט שלמים מערב יום טוב לשמחת לילי יום טוב:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:2:3.english: Or [perhaps] it [comes] only to include the first night of the Festival - And even though there is no offering at night, we learn that Scripture obligated him to slaughter peace-offerings on the eve of the Festival for the rejoicing of the night of the Festival.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:2:4.english: But (joyous) — [the verse] restricts - All [instances of] ach [“but”] and rak [“only”] [indicate] limitations.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:3:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא - משוינן מיעוטא ללילי ראשון וריבויא ללילי אחרון, ולא אמרינן איפכא? לאו משום דאמרינן אין לו במה ישמח, דשלמים הנשחטין מבערב לאו שמחה היא, דבעינן זביחה בשעת שמחה:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:3:1.english: What is the reason - [that] we apply the exclusion to the first night and the inclusion to the last night, and do not say the reverse? Is it not because we say [that] he has nothing with which to rejoice, for peace-offerings that are slaughtered on the eve [of the Festival] do not constitute rejoicing, since we require slaughter at the time of rejoicing.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:4:1.english: For there is rejoicing preceding it - All the days and nights of the Festival.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:5:1.hebrew: חגיגת י"ד כו' - קס"ד דרב יוסף בששחטה בארבעה עשר קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:5:1.english: The chagigah [offering] of the fourteenth, etc. - Rav Yosef initially assumed that [the baraita] is speaking of [a case] where he slaughtered it on the fourteenth.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:6:1.hebrew: הא מתניתא - בן תימא אמרה לעיל, ולבן תימא איפסילא לה, דהא אמר אין נאכלת אלא ליום ולילה:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:6:1.english: This baraita - Ben Teima stated it above, and according to Ben Teima it becomes disqualified, for he said it is eaten only for a day and a night.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:7:2.hebrew: שחל יום טוב בשבת - ומבערב אין יכול לשחוט, דהא בשעת שמחה בעית:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:7:2.english: When [the first] Festival day falls on Shabbat - And one cannot slaughter [it] on the eve [before], for you require [the slaughter to be] at a time of rejoicing.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:7:3.hebrew: אמר רב הונא - ודאי מקרבן שמחה ליכא אלא שבעה, אלא הא דקתני השמחה שמונה, משמחו בשעירי הרגלים. שעיר החטאת האמור בראשון — שבכל יום היה שעיר בא משל ציבור, וכל חטאות החיצונות נאכלות, וכל קרבן ציבור הקבוע דוחה שבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:7:3.english: Rav Huna said - Certainly, from the offering of rejoicing there are only seven [days]; rather, [as for] that which [the baraita] teaches, "rejoicing [is] eight [days]," one rejoices with the male goats of the Festivals. [This refers to] the sin-offering he-goat stated for the first [day] — for on every day a he-goat was brought from [the funds of] the community, and all outer sin-offerings are eaten, and every communal offering that has a fixed [time] overrides Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:8:1.hebrew: חי נאכלין - אם בא לאוכלו בשבת, לא יאכלנו כי אם חי, דאין צלייתו ובישולו דוחה שבת; ובשר חי אין כאן שמחה:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:8:1.english: [They] are eaten raw - If one comes to eat it on Shabbat, he may only eat it raw, for its roasting and cooking do not override Shabbat; and [with] raw meat there is no rejoicing here.

Rashi on Pesachim 71a:8:2.hebrew: ועוד - נהי נמי דיש שמחה בבשר חי, הרי חטאות אין נאכלות אלא לכהנים, והן אוכלין, וישראל במה ישמחו:
Rashi on Pesachim 71a:8:2.english: And furthermore - Even granted that there is rejoicing with raw meat, behold, sin-offerings are eaten only by the priests; thus they eat [them], and with what will Israelites rejoice?

Tosafot on Pesachim 71a:12:1.english: From where [is it derived] that the sacrificial parts of the Festival peace-offering are disqualified when left overnight, as it is stated: "Neither shall [the fat of my Festival offering] be left over," etc. - From here it is derived for all sacrificial parts:

Tosafot on Pesachim 71a:2:1.hebrew: או אינו אלא לילי י"ט הראשון - ולא בא למעוטי שאר לילות, אלא לילי יום טוב האחרון:
Tosafot on Pesachim 71a:2:1.english: Or is it only the night of the first day of the Festival - And [it] does not come to exclude the other nights, [but] only the night of the last day of the Festival.

Tosafot on Pesachim 71a:3:1.hebrew: לאו משום דאין לו במה ישמח - וא"ת: אם כן, תיפוק ליה מאידך קרא דבעינן זביחה בשעת שמחה? וי"ל דאי מהתם ה"א דלא בעינן זביחה בשעת שמחה אלא בחגיגה של יום טוב, שיכול לשוחטה בו ביום, אבל הכא שאין יכול לשוחטה בלילה — לא; להכי איצטריך אך למעט:
Tosafot on Pesachim 71a:3:1.english: "Is it not because he has nothing with which to rejoice?" - And if you say: If so, let it be derived from the other verse, [which teaches] that we require slaughtering at the time of rejoicing? And one can say that if [we derived it] from there, I would have said that we do not require slaughtering at the time of rejoicing except for a chagigah offering of Yom Tov, which one is able to slaughter on that same day; but here [on the first night], when one cannot slaughter it at night, [I would have said] no [it is not required]. Therefore, [the word] ach ["only"] is needed to exclude [it].

Tosafot on Pesachim 71a:4:1.hebrew: לילי יום טוב האחרון - פי' בקונטר': דווקא לילה, אבל יום שמיני לא. וקשה לריב"א, דהתנן: "ההלל והשמחה שמונה", וליכא למימר משום ליל שמיני קתני שמונה, דליכא שמונה לילות — דליל יום טוב ראשון לא קחשיב; ועוד, דומיא דהלל דעיקרו ביום; ועוד, דכי פריך לקמן: "ואם איתא זימנין דלא משכחת לה שמונה, כגון שחל להיות יום טוב הראשון בשבת" — ואי כפירוש הקונט', תיקשי נמי לכולי עלמא, דכשחל יום שמיני באחד בשבת, אז ליכא אלא שבעה! דמתי יוכל לשחוט לליל שמיני שהוא מוצאי שבת? דאי שחיט בערב שבת, איפסלא לה. הלכך נראה לפרש דלילי יום טוב האחרון לאו דווקא, דה"ה ביום:
Tosafot on Pesachim 71a:4:1.english: "The last night of the Festival" - Rashi (the Kuntres) explained: specifically the night, but not the eighth day. And this is difficult for Riba: for we learned in a Mishnah: "The Hallel and the rejoicing are eight [days]." And one cannot say that it teaches "eight" because of the eighth night, for there are not eight nights — since the night of the first day of the Festival is not counted! Furthermore, [rejoicing is] similar to Hallel, whose primary [obligation] is by day. Furthermore, when [the Gemara] asks below: "And if it is so, sometimes you do not find eight [days], such as when the first day of the Festival falls on Shabbat" — if [it is] according to Rashi's explanation, it would also be difficult according to everyone: for when the eighth day falls on Sunday, then there are only seven [days]! For when could one slaughter [the peace-offering] for the eighth night, which is Saturday night? For if one slaughters [it] on Friday, it becomes disqualified [by the eighth night]. Therefore, it appears [correct] to explain that "the last night of the Festival" is not meant strictly [to exclude the day], for the same applies by day.
